scope: Calendar container trash, restore, purge, durable subscription lifecycle pause and detached snapshot cleanup; not full source purge or M4 acceptance
verifiedBehavior: Container trash hides all available members together and removes occurrence coverage; restore preserves identities and independent member deletions.
Trash fences active fetches and rejects late snapshot writes; a source cannot resume while its container is unavailable.
A lifecycle pause survives configured startup reconciliation and restore until an explicit resume.
Member purge retains owned container originals; container purge removes current and historical owned originals, scrubs member payloads and purges projections.
Before-finalize and after-index-commit interruption recovery is idempotent; stale pre-purge publication fences are rejected.
Bounded orphan cleanup retains active and accepted snapshots, removes never-accepted snapshots, replays a quarantine interruption and preserves external file replacements.
notes: Initial focused test incorrectly expected null for a database NULL returned as DBNull; corrected the assertion to check SQL NULL explicitly.
Initial browser readiness callback did not await asynchronous publication; replaced it with bounded polling of the actual query result and reran successfully.

Review after the first full regression found configured startup could reactivate a trashed container; added a durable lifecycle pause and a restart/reconciliation test, then reran all eight test projects.
The browser run preceded the final storage-only configured restart fix; the final deterministic suite covers that fix.
limitations: Full source-level ?purge=1 remains unimplemented, including source removal revision semantics and never-accepted source cleanup.
Container purge currently retains the existing 1000-file and 64-KiB journal metadata bounds; very large retained snapshot sets still require a scalable purge workflow.
Accepted historical snapshots are intentionally retained until container purge; general retention policy and cleanup are still pending.
M4 production migration, backup/restore/export, enrichment/providers/budgets, release supply-chain and final hardened deployment acceptance remain open.
No production data, configuration, subscriptions or network rules were changed.
